Enactus ARSD · Atma Ram Sanatan Dharma College

Entrepreneurial action that puts people first.

We are the student-led Enactus chapter of ARSD College, University of Delhi — working with artisans, gardeners and communities around our campus to build livelihoods, dignity and well-being.

Explore our projects About the chapter

Currently running

  • Project Kalakaari — livelihoods with artisan communities
  • Project Srijan — gardeners & potters to market
  • Project Samvedna — support & mental-health awareness

Who we are

A student team, working with real communities.

Enactus ARSD is part of the global Enactus network — student teams that use entrepreneurial action to address social challenges. Ours is the chapter of Atma Ram Sanatan Dharma College, University of Delhi.

Our work starts by listening to the people around us: artisans with skills but few buyers, gardeners and potters without a market, and neighbours whose mental well-being is too often overlooked. Then we build entrepreneurial responses together with them — not for them.

Read more about us

Our work

Featured projects

Four continuing ventures, each built around the people it serves.

All projects

Livelihoods

Project Kalakaari

Kalakaari works with artisan communities to create and sell handmade canvas bags — a durable, eco-friendly alternative to plastic — while generating employment for underprivileged women.

Explore the project →

Livelihoods

Project Srijan

Srijan supports local gardeners and potters by helping them reach buyers for their plants and handcrafted pots — from potted-plant combinations sold on campus to curated hampers.

Explore the project →

Health awareness

Project Niramaya

Niramaya began during the COVID-19 pandemic, combining practical hygiene support with education and awareness on mental, physical and emotional well-being.

Explore the project →

Our approach

Listen, build, measure, repeat.

  1. Identify the challenge

    We spend time with a community before designing anything, understanding the problem from their perspective.

  2. Build an entrepreneurial response

    Together with the community we design a venture — a product, a service, a route to market — that can sustain itself.

  3. Work alongside people

    Students coordinate, but the makers and participants are the centre of every project.

Competitions · 1 July 2022

Enactus Nationals 2022: chapter competes with Samvedna and Srijan

In July 2022 the chapter took projects Samvedna and Srijan to Enactus Nationals, joining 16 college-level Enactus societies for a week of presentations and judging.

Grants & partnerships · 1 November 2020

₹50,000 KPMG Business Ethics Grant powers Kalakaari and Srijan

A 2020 grant under the KPMG Business Ethics Grant scheme backed two chapter ventures — the artisan livelihoods of Kalakaari and the gardener-and-potter market built by Srijan.
